blocks.text: Church, Samson was the strongest man in Israel. Before he was born, God set him apart. No razor was ever to touch his head. That long hair was the sign of his vow. And for years he fought the Philistines, who were ruling over God's people.

verses.text: And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

blocks.text: Samson played games with her. Tie me with fresh bowstrings, he said, and he snapped them. New ropes, and he broke them like thread. Weave my hair into the loom, and he got up and walked off with the whole thing. Every time, the Philistines were hiding in the room. Every time, he should have known.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: That is one of the saddest lines in the whole Bible. He did not know the LORD had left him. He thought he could shake loose like always. He did not know God's strength had already gone.

blocks.text: The Philistines threw a big party to praise their god for handing them Samson. They brought him out to laugh at him, and stood him between the pillars of the temple, with thousands watching.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The Bible does not hide Samson's mess. He made choice after choice he should not have made. But at the end, broken and blind, he cried out to God, and God heard him. The book of Hebrews lists Samson among the heroes of faith. Not because he did everything right. Because at the last, he turned around and asked God to remember him.
